# How to use this book {#sec-how-to-use .unnumbered}

## Levels

Each chapter carries a badge.

[Core]{.level-badge .core} chapters cover what most introductory university courses on matrices and linear algebra expect.

[Further]{.level-badge .further} chapters go beyond that, into more advanced material and the methods used in research and industry.

## Routes through the book

You do not need to read the book in order.

The book has six parts, shown in the contents list on the left:

| Part | Chapters |
|:-----|:---------|
| Part I: Matrices and transformations | [1](../part-1/01-matrices.qmd)–[9](../part-1/09-invariant-lines.qmd) |
| Part II: Linear systems | [10](../part-2/10-linear-systems.qmd)–[13](../part-2/13-lu-decomposition.qmd) |
| Part III: Vector spaces | [14](../part-3/14-span-independence.qmd)–[17](../part-3/17-orthogonality-least-squares.qmd) |
| Part IV: Eigenvalues and matrix calculus | [18](../part-4/18-eigenvalues.qmd)–[23](../part-4/23-linear-odes.qmd) |
| Part V: Numerical methods | [24](../part-5/24-floating-point-conditioning.qmd)–[30](../part-5/30-qr-least-squares.qmd) |
| Part VI: Applications | [31](../part-6/31-trusses.qmd)–[42](../part-6/42-input-output.qmd) |

These routes pick out the chapters for common courses and goals.

**Engineering mathematics**

- Part I: Matrices and transformations (Chapters [1](../part-1/01-matrices.qmd)–[9](../part-1/09-invariant-lines.qmd))
- Part II: Linear systems (Chapters [10](../part-2/10-linear-systems.qmd)–[13](../part-2/13-lu-decomposition.qmd))
- Chapters [14](../part-3/14-span-independence.qmd)–[16](../part-3/16-fundamental-subspaces.qmd), span, basis and the null space
- Chapters [18](../part-4/18-eigenvalues.qmd) and [19](../part-4/19-diagonalisation.qmd), eigenvalues and diagonalisation
- Applications: Chapters [31](../part-6/31-trusses.qmd), [32](../part-6/32-circuits.qmd), [34](../part-6/34-graphics-robotics.qmd) and [40](../part-6/40-vibrations.qmd) (trusses, circuits, graphics and robotics, vibrations)

**Numerical methods**

This route builds on earlier material. It assumes Parts I–III and Chapters [18](../part-4/18-eigenvalues.qmd)–[20](../part-4/20-symmetric-matrices.qmd), or an earlier course that covered the same ground.

- Chapter [11](../part-2/11-gaussian-elimination.qmd), Gaussian elimination, and Chapter [13](../part-2/13-lu-decomposition.qmd), LU decomposition
- Chapter [17](../part-3/17-orthogonality-least-squares.qmd), orthogonality and least squares
- Chapter [22](../part-4/22-matrix-calculus.qmd), derivatives with vectors and matrices
- Part V: Numerical methods (Chapters [24](../part-5/24-floating-point-conditioning.qmd)–[30](../part-5/30-qr-least-squares.qmd))
- Application: Chapter [33](../part-6/33-finite-differences.qmd), heat flow and finite differences

**Statistics and data science**

- Chapters [1](../part-1/01-matrices.qmd)–[7](../part-1/07-inverses.qmd), from matrices to inverses
- Chapter [9](../part-1/09-invariant-lines.qmd), invariant lines: a first look at eigenvectors
- Chapters [10](../part-2/10-linear-systems.qmd)–[12](../part-2/12-gauss-jordan-rank.qmd), linear systems, Gaussian elimination and rank
- Part III: Vector spaces (Chapters [14](../part-3/14-span-independence.qmd)–[17](../part-3/17-orthogonality-least-squares.qmd))
- Chapters [18](../part-4/18-eigenvalues.qmd)–[21](../part-4/21-svd-pca.qmd), from eigenvalues to the SVD and PCA
- Chapters [24](../part-5/24-floating-point-conditioning.qmd) and [30](../part-5/30-qr-least-squares.qmd), floating point and conditioning, then QR factorisation and stable least squares
- Applications: Chapter [37](../part-6/37-data-science.qmd), regression and dimensionality reduction, and Chapter [41](../part-6/41-networks.qmd), networks and graphs

**Computing and computer science**

- Part I: Matrices and transformations (Chapters [1](../part-1/01-matrices.qmd)–[9](../part-1/09-invariant-lines.qmd)), including the 3D transformations behind computer graphics
- Part II: Linear systems (Chapters [10](../part-2/10-linear-systems.qmd)–[13](../part-2/13-lu-decomposition.qmd))
- Part III: Vector spaces (Chapters [14](../part-3/14-span-independence.qmd)–[17](../part-3/17-orthogonality-least-squares.qmd))
- Chapters [18](../part-4/18-eigenvalues.qmd)–[21](../part-4/21-svd-pca.qmd), from eigenvalues to the SVD and PCA
- Chapter [22](../part-4/22-matrix-calculus.qmd), derivatives with vectors and matrices: the gradients behind gradient descent and machine learning
- Chapters [24](../part-5/24-floating-point-conditioning.qmd), [26](../part-5/26-cost-sparse.qmd), [29](../part-5/29-eigenvalue-algorithms.qmd) and [30](../part-5/30-qr-least-squares.qmd), floating point and conditioning, cost and sparse systems, eigenvalue algorithms, and QR factorisation
- Applications: Chapters [34](../part-6/34-graphics-robotics.qmd), [35](../part-6/35-markov-pagerank.qmd), [41](../part-6/41-networks.qmd) and [37](../part-6/37-data-science.qmd) (computer graphics and robotics, Markov chains and PageRank, networks and graphs, regression and dimensionality reduction). Chapter [39](../part-6/39-cryptography.qmd), cryptography, needs only Chapters [3](../part-1/03-multiplication.qmd) and [7](../part-1/07-inverses.qmd)

**Physics**

- Part I: Matrices and transformations (Chapters [1](../part-1/01-matrices.qmd)–[9](../part-1/09-invariant-lines.qmd))
- Part II: Linear systems (Chapters [10](../part-2/10-linear-systems.qmd)–[13](../part-2/13-lu-decomposition.qmd))

- Part IV: Eigenvalues and matrix calculus (Chapters [18](../part-4/18-eigenvalues.qmd)–[23](../part-4/23-linear-odes.qmd))
- Chapters [24](../part-5/24-floating-point-conditioning.qmd), [26](../part-5/26-cost-sparse.qmd), [27](../part-5/27-iterative-methods.qmd) and [29](../part-5/29-eigenvalue-algorithms.qmd), conditioning, sparse systems, iterative methods and eigenvalue algorithms, for computational work
- Applications: Chapters [38](../part-6/38-physics.qmd), [33](../part-6/33-finite-differences.qmd) and [40](../part-6/40-vibrations.qmd) (rotations, inertia and quantum states; heat flow and finite differences; vibrations and normal modes)

**Biology and life sciences**

- Chapters [1](../part-1/01-matrices.qmd)–[7](../part-1/07-inverses.qmd), from matrices to inverses

**Economics and business**

- Chapters [1](../part-1/01-matrices.qmd)–[7](../part-1/07-inverses.qmd), from matrices to inverses
- Chapter [9](../part-1/09-invariant-lines.qmd), invariant lines: a first look at eigenvectors
- Part II: Linear systems (Chapters [10](../part-2/10-linear-systems.qmd)–[13](../part-2/13-lu-decomposition.qmd))
- Part III: Vector spaces (Chapters [14](../part-3/14-span-independence.qmd)–[17](../part-3/17-orthogonality-least-squares.qmd)), ending with least squares for fitting models to data
- Chapters [18](../part-4/18-eigenvalues.qmd) and [19](../part-4/19-diagonalisation.qmd), eigenvalues and matrix powers
- Applications: Chapter [42](../part-6/42-input-output.qmd), input–output models, needs only Parts I and II; then Chapter [35](../part-6/35-markov-pagerank.qmd), Markov chains
- For regression, Chapter [37](../part-6/37-data-science.qmd), read Chapters [20](../part-4/20-symmetric-matrices.qmd), [21](../part-4/21-svd-pca.qmd), [24](../part-5/24-floating-point-conditioning.qmd) and [30](../part-5/30-qr-least-squares.qmd) first

## How each chapter works

Chapters follow the same pattern, so you always know where to look.

1. **In this chapter you will** lists what you should be able to do by the end, and **Builds on** names the chapters to revise first if any of their ideas are hazy.
2. **Build intuition** opens with an app, a picture or a small example, using only what you already know. When an app needs the chapter's new ideas, it appears (or reappears) later, next to the idea it illustrates.
3. **The ideas** explains the rules, and why they work. After each idea comes a **worked example**, in a box, that shows the method by hand, step by step. Try it yourself before reading the solution.
4. **In code** shows the same methods in Python and MATLAB.
5. **Check your understanding** has quick questions. Click to reveal each answer.
6. **Key ideas** sums up the chapter in a few points: a quick check before the exercises, and the place to start when you revise.
7. **Exercises** have full solutions in the appendices, one for each Part (@sec-solutions-part-1 to @sec-solutions-part-6). Each exercise ends with a link to its solution, and each solution with a link back. Have a real go at an exercise before following its link: the effort of trying is what makes the solution stick. Exercises marked † are harder: they take longer, or need an idea that the worked examples don't show. Some proofs end with a hint that gives a first step.
8. **In practice** shows where the ideas are used.
9. **Going further** points to deeper material and to the proofs in @sec-proofs.

The application chapters in Part VI start from a real problem instead, and follow a shorter pattern: **The problem** sets the scene, **The model** builds the mathematics with worked examples, **Explore** has an app or a figure to experiment with, and then come the code, a few quick self-test questions, the key ideas, exercises and pointers further.

Each Part ends with a **Part review**: a set of exercises that mixes the ideas of the whole Part, and of earlier Parts, without saying which chapter each one comes from. Deciding which method to use is part of the exercise. This is harder than practising one chapter at a time, but mixing topics in this way makes the ideas last much longer, so the reviews are worth doing when you finish a Part and again before an exam. Their solutions, at the end of each Part's solutions appendix, say which chapters each exercise draws on.

## Using the apps

The apps run in your browser, with nothing to install. Each one also opens in its own tab, which is useful for teaching from a projector, and @sec-apps lists them all in one place. They work with a keyboard and a screen reader as well as a mouse or touchscreen.

## Running the code

The Python examples use [NumPy](https://numpy.org), [SciPy](https://scipy.org) and [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org). The MATLAB examples use only core MATLAB, and also run in the free [GNU Octave](https://octave.org). Copy any example with the button at its top right. If you are new to either language, the [Refresher](refresher.qmd#sec-code-primer) explains how to get set up and the basics you need.
